chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Latin concert at St. Patrick's Cathedral
summary: He organizes a concert with Chico O'Farrill's suite, after church refusals.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So that was my fourth __________, if you call it, or my fourth success or my fourth -- because everything that I wanted up to then, little by little, I created. And when I (unintelligible) concert in St. Patricks, (unintelligible).
Can you talk about that? Because that was the first Afro-Cuban suite to be recorded for a long time, wasn't it, since the '50s.
Yeah, and you know what happened?

Well, I tell you what happened. I was talking to a lady, a friend of mine. (Unintelligible) they've never given to the Latin people. St. George's is only for the white rich people, the classy white people. So I said, so I need somebody to help me. How can we do something? I said, you want to do something? Come with me. I like everything (inaudible). All you got to do, try to get the church. If you get the church, forget about the music and the performers. I'll provide that.
We ain't got no money. I said, forget about the money. So Chico and I --

Chico got a thing he wrote for (inaudible). So I said, Chico, I have a chance to do something (inaudible). He say, (inaudible). I say, regardless of what happens, I'm going to record (inaudible). So this lady (inaudible). So they told her, no, no, no, we cannot accept that. If we do bring a concert (inaudible). So she wrote to the department of culture in Spain. (Unintelligible.) We go back again, no. (Inaudible) directly to the Pope and tell him the question and what are we doing.
So the reaction was good. The Pope said, no, no, no, nothing can be done (unintelligible) they have to give us a day. So we said, all right. So you got to make a more classical
I said, great. So I say we're going to divide this in two ways. Let's get a (unintelligible) from Puerto Rico. She's a big star.
Ruth Hernandez. We got (unintelligible) who is a big soprano in Puerto Rico, the outstanding soprano in Puerto Rico. We got (unintelligible) from Cuba.

Jomana Alfarro from Cuba. I got a piano player that just came out of Juillard, this lady got a choir from the Juillard. So we combined all that (inaudible). That was the biggest explosion you ever see in New York City. On Channel two and Channel 37, they were supposed to come on with the news. I don't know what happened. (Unintelligible). The New York Times said, the first time in history, (unintelligible).
